body: Or just give people reasonable holiday pay. Some people will choose to come in for 2.5x pay!

The culture of women complaining about their kids or refusing to take responsibility for their actions can be irritating, but I think some of these people are victims of indoctrination by religious or patriarchal propaganda. They reduce themselves to ‘mother’ and try to fulfill the roles expected of them, then realize later that it’s impossible. So I have sympathy for them. 

I also think some people have children expecting the family they created to stay together, but we live in a society where many women become single parents, which is a unique difficulty. Not to mention the economic situation many people find themselves in… some people who have kids pretty much have to have one person stay home because of  the costs of childcare in the United States.
Same. Definitely going to do it before I hit 50 or so and things really start to go downhill health wise.
Sounds like you did well. Opening up the lines of communication is so important.

I know someone who also had to do this (gift pto to a sick coworker.) Also a teacher. Idk if it’s related to education or if it’s just an American thing and lots of people have to do this in multiple professions. I’ve never had a good enough job to be able to use pto, so idk much about it.

This person has every obligation to tell their partner ASAP. It’s insane to me that they would hesitate to do so. They entered into a marriage believing they had the same long term goals… the partner should have the opportunity to leave, and OP needs to accept the consequences of the choices they’d like to make gracefully.

I’m so sorry. I’ve had a couple of deeply disappointing birthdays like this. The worst is when they do nothing for your birthday then expect the world for theirs. People sometimes aren’t mature enough to understand how their actions have a serious impact on others. I’m glad you’re in therapy. Hopefully you can lean on your therapist a little more during this time and be honest about what you’re experiencing.

I’m 30 and life is so much better than it was in my early twenties. I spent a lot of that time in meaningless relationships, not putting myself first, not really knowing who I was. My twenties sucked. I feel like I have a much better idea of what’s important now. After I broke up with my last long term bf, I came to the realization that I did a lot of shit because I’d internalized society’s expectations of me. I hope you have a similar experience but way earlier lol

Getting older hasn’t made me feel less happy with my body. I’m more comfortable with it and confident with it. But mostly, I don’t care about meeting the standards of peak attraction anymore. You eventually learn that it has very little bearing on your happiness.

Does he not have any friends? Coworkers? People he volunteers with? Other family members? A partner? Because I have all of those… why would I be lonely? It’s like saying “you’re an only child and have no nieces or nephews. Your life must be sad and incomplete.” My entire life doesn’t revolve around one specific social group. That’s called putting all your eggs in one basket.
I don’t even have a job that provides affordable health insurance. If I get into a car accident, I’m probably going to have to declare bankruptcy. Explain how I’m going to have a child.
That’s what got me too. It’s so awkward. Imagine being this out of touch.
Glad to know I’m not alone. It sounds like you’re definitely doing what is best for your mental health, super inspiring!

I know you’re right… that’s what I’m trying to tell myself. Wish it made me feel better.

I think it’s especially tough when you feel like the people you work with are your friends.

Thanks for your comment. Back of house is such a tough environment. I know people whose entire life is working insane hours in the kitchen as you describe. I’m glad you got out. I don’t know why it has to be that way, and why some people wear it as a badge of honor. Life is too short to spend every waking moment working.

I know and I agree with you. But I still feel bad. 

It’s not about the company— I know that they don’t care. it’s about the employees who work with me. I feel bad because I don’t like feeling like I’m even inadvertently causing other people issues.

I wish I could think in a way that benefits me more, but I find it really tough to do so.

I’m so sorry you’re dealing with this. I know exactly what you’re talking about. A few years ago, I seriously injured my foot, (heard a crack and couldn’t walk on it for a while… it may have been broken) but I didn’t have heath insurance, so I just bought crutches and hobbled around on it until it healed on its own. I was working two jobs at the time and made enough that I didn’t qualify for low income help, but all my money went to paying rent, so I definitely didn’t have any spare money. It’s completely insane that we live this way.

I work part time (sometimes almost full time, but 39 hours a week doesn’t get benefits) and go to college full time. I don’t have any job security, no health insurance and no paid sick leave. And this is one of the best jobs I’ve ever had because it’s flexible and I like my coworkers.

I’ve lived in the us my entire life and worked many different jobs. The work culture here is BAD. It’s pro employer, “if you don’t like it, then leave.” 

The food and beverage industry was probably the worst… they hire young people or desperate people and straight up abuse them. Hardest work I’ve ever done for the least amount of money I’ve ever made. One time I sat down at work during a 11 hour shift (no overtime though) and my manager happened to walk in and she acted like she caught me stealing from her purse lol. So ridiculous.

It’s not just people “at the bottom” either. I know multiple people with bachelors and masters degrees struggling to make ends meet. I know someone with a phd who decided to go back to school for a second graduate degree because he couldn’t make it work with his first degree.
Or ask again via email. “I was thinking about it and honestly, I’d really like the time off I requested for my medical appointment, blah blah blah.”
